supporting_evidence.quote: Gross margin decreased 160 basis points to 49.8% of net sales for the quarter. The decrease in gross margin was due to: • 140 basis points of higher commodity costs
The gross margin decline of 90 basis points was driven by the higher cost of commodities and unfavorable product mix

input.reasoning_summary: The claim states that higher commodity costs were one of the main drivers of the decline in P&G's gross margin in the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Evidence E2, which is from the 10-Q filed on 2026-10-22 for the period ending 2026-09-30, explicitly states that gross margin decreased 160 basis points for the quarter, and lists "140 basis points of higher commodity costs" as the first and largest contributor to this decline. This represents 140 out of 350 total basis points of negative impacts (before offsets), making it the joint-largest contributor along with product and packaging investments. Evidence E4 from the same filing also confirms that "the higher cost of commodities" was a driver of the gross margin decline. Therefore, the claim is fully supported - both the numeric assertion about the gross margin decline and the attribution to higher commodity costs as a main driver are confirmed by the evidence.
